title.narrative: Portfolio guarantee Kenya Support Refugee owned MSMEs

description.narrative: Med denna insats (portföljgaranti) är målet att Sida ska öka tillgången till finansiering för mikro, små och medelstora företag, MSME, privatpersoner och Village Savings and Lending Associations, VSLAs. Ett särskilt fokus kommer att vara att möjliggöra finansiering till företag som ägs av flyktingar, utlåning till MSMEer med KCB:s islamiska bankprodukt och konventionell utlåning och möjliggöra finansiering till MSMEer i relevanta sektorer som ägs av kvinnor och ungdomar. Det övergripande syftet är förbättrad tillgång till finansiering, skapande av arbetstillfällen och förbättrad övergripande ekonomisk tillväxt. Sidas strategi i Kenya anger att man ska fokusera på bättre villkor för produktiv sysselsättning, anständiga arbetsvillkor och större ekonomiskt egenmakt, särskilt för kvinnor, unga och marginaliserade grupper inklusive flyktingar.

With this contribution (portfolio guarantee) Sida aims to increase access to finance for micro, small and medium sized companies, MSMEs, individuals and Village Savings and Lending Associations, VSLAs. A particular focus will be to enable financing to the companies owned by refugees, lending to MSME's with KCB's Islamic banking product and conventional lending and enabling financing to MSMEs in relevant sectors owned by women and youth. The overall purpose is enhancement of access to finance, job creation and improved overall economic growth. The Sida’s Strategy in Kenya stipulates to focus on better conditions for productive employment, decent working conditions and greater economic empowerment, especially for women, young people and marginalized groups including refugees.

The contribution is a guarantee program that is aimed to leverage private capital to support the development objectives of the Swedish Development strategy in Kenya. The strategy envisages a guarantee with KCB Bank in Kenya targeting access to finance for micro, small and medium sized companies, MSMEs, individuals and Village Savings and Lending Associations, VSLAs. A particular focus will be (i) enabling financing to the businesses owned by refugees, lending to MSMEs with KCB's Islamic banking product and conventional lending and (ii) enabling financing to MSMEs in relevant sectors owned by women, youth and for the start up companies. The overall purpose is enhancement of access to finance, job creation and improved overall economic growth.
The proposed intervention falls under the Strategy for Sweden'ss development cooperation with Kenya, 2021-2025. The support area relevant for this contribution is Economic development and protection systems that include the most vulnerable. The guarantee is also planned to be relevant for the support of the other two areas of the strategy, Climate change, the environment and resilience in the face of climate change and Human rights, democracy, rule of law, gender equality and sexual and reproductive health and rights.

The year 2024 started with high level meeting at KCB Bank on 01/02/2024 where the delegation of the three Director Generals from the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs were accompanied by H.E. Ambassador Caroline Vicini. The DGs were Mr. Dag Juhlin Dannfelt, Director General for Global Affairs; Ms. Helen Eduards, Director General for Global Affairs; Mr. Per-Arne Hjelmborn, Director General for International Trade. the goal of this meeting was to discuss the role of the financial sector for the development agenda, the role of innovative financing and guarantees from donors, the migration and refugee situation in Kenya and the region, the trade and investments opportunities, and green/climate financing.
KCB received approvals from CBK to launch the refugee product and the loan disbursements to the refugee and host communities commenced. One of the initial target groups were urban refugees, however, during the year we had camp-based refugee and host community borrowers in Kakuma nad Kalobeyei also accessing the guarantee facility. The current range of amounts borrowed is between Ksh 50,000 and Ksh 10,000,000. As at 31st December 2024 the total loan amount disbursed was Ksh. 28,713,187 which is equivalent to 3% of the total guarantee volume of Ksh.1 billion. Further analaysis shows 32% of loans have been issued to refugees and 68% to the host community. The reports are not presented based on gender and this is an area of discussion for future reports.
As a way to widen the KYC requirements. KCB has granted the use of a manifest ( a document issued by Department for Refugee Affairs/ Refugee Affairs Secretariat (RAS) that attest to refugee registration in a camp/urban centre). KCB Bank has also allowed for opening of joint accounts by CSLA leaders/signatories. These accounts shall then be upgraded to group accounts once the CSLAs acquire formal registration documents. (Please see attached circular)
In June 2025, KCB held a sensitisation workshop for its relationship managers in collaboration with DRC. The workshop aimed to raise awareness about the guarantee program, refugee lending and train managers on how to effectively handle refugees as customers. This initiative highlights KCB's commitment to supporting all customers, including refugees.
In October, Sida HQ Garanalys and embassy PM carried out an introduction meeting with KCB Bank with the goal of clarify the terms of the agreement. Several issues were raised during the meeting, please see clarification document attached. The areas highlighted include: VSLA/GROUPS- Borrowing process by DRC groups, green financing, lending to MSMEs including all the MSMEs across all the sectors, does gurantee support invoice discounting, LPO financing, short term accommodations, Overdraft facilities, Top up loans & Repeat customers and conditions under Women and youth.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
